rules.sentence: If the patient is suffering from complications of bronchial atresia, it is imperative to seek medical treatment.
Most cases are found incidentally on radiography with high-resolution computed tomography being the modality of choice for diagnosis.
Treatment and management are controversial with asymptomatic patients being managed conservatively or undergoing surgery to prevent long-term outcomes.
If the patient is asymptomatic, the healthcare team must discuss conservative management versus elective surgery.
If the patient is suffering from severe effects from bronchial atresia, early consultation with thoracic surgery and pulmonology is necessary.
